record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in Dynamical Systems
record.original_question: On the complement G^1_ψ(M) \ SE^1_ψ, which side of the entropy dichotomy analogous to Question 4.3 holds: generic zero maximal Lyapunov exponent, or instead a nonempty open region of uniformly positive entropy?

evidence.quote: On G1ψ(M) \ SE1ψ, which of the two possibilities of 4.3 is true ?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed symplectic manifold of dimension $2d \ge 2$ with symplectic form $\omega$. Fix a smooth Hamiltonian-type function (or, more generally, a cohomology class) $\psi$, and consider the space $G^1_\psi(M)$ of $C^1$ symplectomorphisms of $M$ preserving $\psi$ (equivalently, the $C^1$ closure of an appropriate class of $\psi$-preserving symplectic diffeomorphisms), endowed with the $C^1$ topology. Inside $G^1_\psi(M)$ let $SE^1_\psi$ denote the (open) subset of stably ergodic, or more precisely, stably-nonzero-exponent diffeomorphisms — those $f$ admitting a $C^1$ neighborhood on which every element has all Lyapunov exponents (with respect to the invariant volume) bounded away from zero almost everywhere.

For $f \in G^1_\psi(M)$ let $\lambda^+_{\max}(f,x)$ denote the largest Lyapunov exponent at a point $x$, and let $\Lambda^+_{\max}(f) = \int \lambda^+_{\max}(f,x)\,d\mathrm{vol}(x)$.

Consider the complement $G^1_\psi(M) \setminus SE^1_\psi$. Decide which of the following alternatives holds:

(a) There is a $C^1$-residual subset $\mathcal{R} \subset G^1_\psi(M) \setminus SE^1_\psi$ on which the maximal Lyapunov exponent vanishes almost everywhere, i.e. $\lambda^+_{\max}(f,x) = 0$ for vol-a.e. $x$ and every $f \in \mathcal{R}$ (equivalently, the metric entropy of $f$ with respect to volume is zero);

(b) There exists a nonempty $C^1$-open set $\mathcal{U} \subset G^1_\psi(M) \setminus SE^1_\psi$ and a constant $c > 0$ such that the topological entropy (or the volume-metric entropy) of every $f \in \mathcal{U}$ is at least $c$.

Determine which of (a) or (b) is true.
artifact.category_tag: Lyapunov exponents and entropy of symplectic diffeomorphisms
artifact.status_search_result: No published resolution of this dichotomy on the complement of the stable-exponent set within the space of $\psi$-preserving symplectic $C^1$ diffeomorphisms was found. Related generic results (e.g. Bochi–Viana on zero exponents being $C^1$-generic among volume-preserving systems, and dichotomies for partially hyperbolic systems) address adjacent settings but do not settle this specific question.

status_evidence.title: On Herman's Positive Entropy Conjecture
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses open conjectures concerning positive entropy in symplectic/volume-preserving settings near elliptic regimes.
status_evidence.claim: Related dichotomies between zero exponents and positive entropy in conservative dynamics remain active open problems.

status_evidence.title: Lyapunov exponents and entropy for divergence-free Lipschitz vector fields
status_evidence.snippet: Studies generic Lyapunov-exponent/entropy dichotomies for conservative systems.
status_evidence.claim: Generic dichotomies in conservative C^1 settings are studied but the specific question on G^1_psi \ SE^1_psi is not resolved.
